forces: Nothing implements the SDK sink boundary over HTTP, so every developer hand-writes the glue between the SDK and the Node binding's delivery pieces.
The delivery handoff's request projection overwrites correlation.retry_attempt, so a sink built on it cannot send the validated event byte for byte.
CONTRIBUTING.md requires every transport to have its own OpenSpec change and explicit authorization, never an incidental addition.
The Node surface is frozen and widens only additively through a governed change that updates the frozen lists, the freeze record and an ADR together.
Only src/fetch-exchange.ts may reach fetch, and the scope gate rejects tokens such as transport, adapter and collector in source file names.
Two rule sets for classifying HTTP responses, one in the handoff and one in a sink, would drift apart.
Developers must correlate a failed send with their own logs and the receiver's, which needs the event identifier.
The ratified F-11 requirement forbids event IDs in sink-failure diagnostics and coherence freezes it byte for byte.
The delivery peer is untrusted: it can stall, refuse, redirect, or answer with malformed or ambiguous acknowledgments, and none of those may become acceptance.

approach-handoff-backed-sink.reason: The handoff's projection rewrites correlation.retry_attempt, which breaks the byte-exact body the evaluation depends on, and its attempt semantics imply a delivery-class conformance the sink does not claim.

forces: Two rule sets for classifying HTTP responses, one in the handoff and one in a sink, would drift apart.
approach-sink-local-classification.reason: Two copies of the status and acknowledgment rules would drift, so a status such as 429 could be a failure in one component and a rejection in the other; one shared classifier keeps a single source of classification.

security_justification.audit_integrity: The sink sends exactly the validated event bytes and reports acceptance only for the one exact acknowledgment, so no field is rewritten and no failure becomes a delivered state.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: The sink holds no credential of its own; caller headers are sent only to the configured origin and never follow a redirect.
security_justification.authority_provenance: The sink forwards the SDK-validated event unchanged, so authoritative and claimed values keep the distinction the SDK gave them.
security_justification.concurrency: Concurrent emits are allowed with no ordering promise; each request is independent and settles once, and flush tracks only requests started before it.
security_justification.confidentiality: Events go only to the configured origin with no redirect following, headers are never logged or echoed, and the outcome callback never receives bodies, payloads or header values.
security_justification.cryptography: No cryptography is implemented; https origins use the runtime's TLS without configuration by the sink.
security_justification.error_disclosure: Core sink-failure diagnostics keep F-11's bounded fields with no event identifier; the callback reports only the event identifier, a closed code and a status.
security_justification.external_security_integration: The sink reaches only the configured origin through the governed fetch adapter and adds no dependency.
security_justification.fail_posture: Invalid options throw at construction, and every ambiguous, malformed, redirected or timed-out response maps to failure rather than acceptance.
security_justification.lifecycle: flush waits for in-flight requests and SDK shutdown drains them within its bound before the sink closes; emits after shutdown return SDK_SHUT_DOWN.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: Changes are confined to the exact sdk-node paths in owned_paths and the canonical Node capability through the fold; no CB-018-owned or governance-core path is touched.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: The sink transforms no field; privacy transformation stays in the SDK before validation, and the evaluation is synthetic-data only.
security_justification.resource_retention: The sink retains only the set of in-flight requests; responses are read to the adapter's bound and discarded.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: The sink never retries, batches or queues; one attempt per emit is the documented guarantee, and correlation.retry_attempt is sent exactly as validated.
security_justification.trust_boundary: The receiving peer is untrusted; the shared classifier reduces its behaviour to a closed code set, and nothing it sends becomes acceptance except the exact acknowledgment.
